title: Simultaneous Cohen ambient lift of two tame rigidifications
statement:
Let $X=\coprod_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ be a finite disjoint union of spectra of complete Noetherian regular local rings with separably closed residue fields [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Let a finite group $G$ act tamely, freely outside a $G$-strict strict normal crossings boundary $B$, with abelian geometric inertia. Geometric inertia means the stabilizer of a geometric point, tame means that its order is invertible in the residue field, and $G$-strict means distinct translates of each irreducible boundary component are disjoint. Let $D_1,D_2$ be invariant normal crossings divisors containing $B$, whose divisorial fs log structures are very tame [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Here normal crossings means etale locally a product of distinct regular parameters, and very tame means that inertia acts trivially on the characteristic monoid and on the strict local log stratum.

There are $G$-equivariant maps $h:U\to X$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$, with $h$ surjective etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $j$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and invariant strict normal crossings divisors $E\subset E_1,E_2$ on a Noetherian regular separated scheme $Y$, with these properties. As a scheme over $X$, $U$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of the components $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, each mapping isomorphically onto that component. Both maps induce isomorphisms on all geometric inertia groups. Scheme-theoretically, $j^{-1}E=h^{-1}B$ and $j^{-1}E_a=h^{-1}D_a$ for $a=1,2$, so $j$ is strict for each of the three divisorial log structures. The action on $Y$ is tame, has abelian geometric inertia, and is free outside the $G$-strict divisor $E$; both $(Y,E_a)$ are very tame fs log regular schemes. Both $Y$ and $Q=Y/G$ are finite disjoint unions of integral affine schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The two log quotients have this same underlying scheme $Q$; their log structures $M_a=(q_*M_{E_a})^G$ are fs log regular. Every generic point of every log stratum of $(Q,M_1)$ and $(Q,M_2)$ has residue characteristic zero. A log stratum here is a connected component of the locus where the rank of the group completion of the characteristic monoid is constant [def-trf-fs-log-blowup].

The local ambient pieces in residue characteristic $p>0$ may be chosen as spectra of $C(k)[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]$, with $C(k)$ a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and two systems of boundary-adapted eigenparameters lifting those on $A_i$. In residue characteristic zero the pieces may be taken to be the original complete local schemes. The construction allows $m=0$, dimension zero, empty boundaries, and permutation of components by $G$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.5.2, proof, pp.127--128: invariant Cohen coefficients, two weighted-averaged parameter systems, their simultaneous ambient lift, and the final disjoint-union paragraph. Inertia induction is the construction of VIII 5.3.6--5.3.7, pp.124--125.

proof.text: Reduce to closed geometric inertia, keeping track of the eventual cover. Choose one component $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$ in each $G$-orbit of components, its closed point $x$, and $H\leq G$ the stabilizer of a geometric point over $x$. Any geometric inertia at a point of $X_i$ is contained in $H$: an element fixing that geometric point preserves the component, and $g(a)-a$ lies in its prime ideal for all $a\in A$, hence lies in the maximal ideal, so $g$ is trivial on the closed residue field. Thus $H$ is abelian, fixes $k$, and $N=|H|$ is a unit in $A$. We construct an $H$-equivariant closed embedding of $X_i$ into a local ambient piece. At the end we induce each such piece from $H$ to $G$. For residue characteristic zero take the ambient piece to be $X_i$ itself. Regular local rings and all their localizations are regular domains by the cited statements, so these pieces are integral and regular.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.127, reduction to H=G_x; VIII 5.3.7, p.124, induction of actions

proof.text: $A$ is henselian by the complete-pair theorem, hence strictly henselian. Take an affine pointed etale chart $(V,v)\to X_i$ at the closed point where $D_a$ is a product of distinct regular parameters of $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Its residue field is finite separable over $k$, hence $k$, so the henselian retraction gives a section $s:X_i\to V$ through $v$, a clopen immersion as $V$ is separated; thus $A=\mathcal O_{V,v}$ and $D_a=V(w_1\cdots w_n)$ with $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ part of a regular system of parameters of $A$. Check the strict-normal-crossings definition: for $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $(w_j)_{j\in J}$ is a regular sequence and $A/(w_j:j\in J)$ is regular local of dimension $\dim A-|J|$, hence a domain with regular localizations, so each $C_J$ is integral and regular. At a prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq(w_J)$ the localized sequence stays regular and the dimension formula gives $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=\dim\mathcal O_{C_J,\mathfrak p}+|J|$. The product is a nonzerodivisor, and $(w_1\cdots w_n)=\bigcap_j(w_j)$ by induction: if $c=w_1b$ lies in every $(w_j)$, then for $j\ge2$ the prime $(w_j)$ does not contain $w_1$ (independent cotangent classes), so $b\in\bigcap_{j\ge2}(w_j)=(w_2\cdots w_n)$. So $D_a$ is a strict normal crossings boundary, and each component of $B$, an integral codimension-one closed subset of $|D_a|$, is one of its branches. The regular-boundary chart statement then gives the chart $\mathbf N^n$ at $x$, with branch equations having independent cotangent lines. Inertia $H$ fixes each branch of $D_a$ since it fixes the characteristic monoid. Its branches belonging to $B$ are the same for the two divisors.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, strictness over strictly henselian local rings; VI 1.2--1.5

proof.text: Now suppose $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. Choose a Cohen ring $C$ with residue field $k$. Construct a map $C\to A^H$ without assuming an invariant coefficient section in advance. Put $R_n=(A/\mathfrak m^n)^H$. Averaging with $N^{-1}\sum_hh$ shows $R_n\to R_{n-1}$ is surjective; its kernel is square-zero for $n\geq2$, and $p^nR_n=0$. Starting with $C/p\simeq R_1=k$, formal smoothness of $C/p^n$ over $\mathbf Z/p^n$ lifts the composite $C/p^n\to C/p^{n-1}\to R_{n-1}$ to $R_n$ compatibly for every $n$. Completeness $A=\varprojlim A/\mathfrak m^n$ gives the required invariant local map $C\to A$. Both $C$ and $A$ are henselian. Apply the cyclotomic finite etale cover and the henselian retraction to $C$: separable closedness of $k$ supplies a point with residue $k$, so $C$ contains an $H$-fixed primitive $N$th root $\zeta$ with every $1-\zeta^a$ a unit. Its image has the same properties in $A$.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, pp.127--128, invariant Cohen coefficients; Stacks 0328, 0329, 032A

proof.text: Choose equations for the branches of $B$ and apply the character projector to each. Its principal ideal is $H$-stable, so the projector stays in that ideal and preserves its nonzero cotangent class; the new equation is therefore a unit multiple of the old one. Keep these same equations $z_1,\ldots,z_l$ for both divisors. For each $D_a$, do the same with its other branch equations, and extend their independent cotangent eigenvectors to an eigenbasis. Lift and project the remaining basis vectors. Nakayama applied to the finitely generated maximal ideal, and the regular cotangent-dimension statement, show that these lists are regular parameter systems $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)$ and $z'=(z'_1,\ldots,z'_d)$, with common first $l$ entries, and $D_1=V(\prod_{i\leq n_1}z_i)$, $D_2=V(\prod_{i\leq n_2}z'_i)$. All characters take values in $\langle\zeta\rangle$. The projector formula is applied to the semilinear modules $A$ and $\mathfrak m$, not to an assumed linear action on $A$ over $k$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.5, p.124, and VIII 5.5.2, p.128, two parameter systems

proof.text: Set $R=C[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]$ and let $f:R\to A$ send $t_i$ to $z_i$ and use the invariant coefficient map of Step 3. The power-series evaluation theorem constructs $f$. It is local, induces the identity on $k$, and is surjective on cotangent spaces because the $z_i$ generate $\mathfrak m$. The complete-local cotangent-surjectivity theorem therefore makes $f$ surjective. Give $R$ the continuous diagonal $H$-action fixing $C$ and sending $t_i$ to $\chi_i(h)t_i$; evaluating a monomial shows $f$ is equivariant, hence evaluating the convergent degree truncations shows the same for every series. The ambient local ring $R$ is Noetherian, complete, regular and integral by the field/Cohen power-series theorem. Its spectrum is regular by regular-local localization. Apply the relative-coordinate-lift node to obtain $t'_i$ lifting $z'_i$, with $t'_i=t_i$ for $i\leq l$, and $R=C[[t'_1,\ldots,t'_d]]$ over the same $C$, equivariantly.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, the surjection B->A and simultaneous parameter lift

proof.text: On $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$ put $E=V(\prod_{i\leq l}t_i)$, $E_1=V(\prod_{i\leq n_1}t_i)$ and $E_2=V(\prod_{i\leq n_2}t'_i)$. Each coordinate intersection is a Cohen power-series ring by the variable-quotient theorem, also for the primed system by its $C$-algebra coordinate isomorphism. These rings are regular domains, and their localizations are regular. A coordinate sublist is a regular sequence; its localization at a prime containing it remains regular, and the regular-sequence dimension formula gives the codimension equal to its length at every point. The product of distinct coordinate variables is a nonzerodivisor and its ideal is the intersection of their prime ideals: coefficientwise, divisibility by each variable means divisibility by their product. Thus the finite coordinate components and intersections satisfy precisely the strict-normal-crossings definition. Invariance follows from their eigenvector equations; each component is individually $H$-stable. The regular-boundary chart statement makes both enlarged pairs fs log regular. Scheme-theoretic inverse images are the indicated original products. The charts $\mathbf N^l$ and $\mathbf N^{n_a}$ pull back by the very same equations, proving strictness of $j_i:\operatorname{Spec}A\hookrightarrow Y_i$ for all three structures.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, the three lifted divisors; VIII 4.2.2(i), p.118

proof.text: For each nonidentity $g\in H$, let $I_g=\{i:\chi_i(g)\ne1\}$. The ideal of differences $g(a)-a$ in $A$ is exactly $J_g=(z_i:i\in I_g)$: one inclusion uses the generators, whose nontrivial character differences are units, and the other follows by setting the same variables equal to zero in a power series preimage under $f$. The quotient $A/J_g$ is a regular local domain, by the parameter-quotient and regular-domain results. Consequently $J_g$ is prime, and $g$ fixes every geometric point of its spectrum. Freeness on $X_i\setminus B$ forces $\prod_{i\leq l}z_i\in J_g$. Primality, and independence of the parameter classes, give an index $i\leq l$ in $I_g$. On $R$, a geometric fixed point of $g$ must have $t_i=0$ for this index. Thus $H$ acts freely on $Y_i\setminus E$. Its geometric inertia groups are subgroups of the abelian group $H$, and their orders are units since $N$ is a unit in $C$. The map $j_i$ is inert: if $g j_i(\bar u)=j_i(\bar u)$, equivariance and the monomorphism $j_i$ give $g\bar u=\bar u$; the reverse implication is immediate.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, the lifted tame action and strict inert immersion; VIII 5.3.6

proof.text: The two lifted actions are very tame. For the unprimed system, very tameness on $A$ says $H$ fixes $A/(z_1,\ldots,z_{n_1})$. Each remaining $z_i$ has nonzero cotangent class in this quotient, so its character must be trivial (a nontrivial root minus $1$ is a unit). Hence $H$ fixes $R/(t_1,\ldots,t_{n_1})=C[[t_{n_1+1},\ldots,t_d]]$ pointwise. It also fixes the characteristic monoid at the closed point since each coordinate divisor is invariant, and is tame there. The closed residue field of $R$ is separably closed and $R$ is complete henselian, so each pointed affine etale neighborhood admits the unique residue-preserving retraction. These retractions identify their colimit, the strict local ring, with $R$. This proves very tameness at its closed point. The affine scheme $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: its diagonal is the closed immersion induced by the surjective multiplication map $R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}R\to R$. Thus the separatedness hypothesis of the very-tame-locus theorem holds; its other hypotheses are the Noetherian fs log regularity from Steps 5--6 and the finite log action from the invariant divisors. The very-tame locus is therefore open; an open subset containing the closed point of a local spectrum is the whole spectrum. Repeat with $t'$ and $n_2$ for $E_2$. In characteristic zero the chosen ambient scheme and its two log structures were the original ones, already very tame.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, trivial characters off the enlarged boundary; VIII 5.3.2(i)

proof.text: Each local ambient scheme is affine and integral. Apply the very-tame log-quotient theorem separately to its two fs log regular structures; its admissibility hypothesis holds since it is affine, and generic freeness holds by Step 7 (or the original free complement in characteristic zero). Both applications have the same underlying categorical scheme quotient $Q_i=Y_i/H$, with invariant log structures and finite surjective quotient map having orbit geometric fibres. Both log structures are fs log regular and both quotient maps are Kummer etale. The affine-quotient statement identifies $Q_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$ (with $R=A$ in characteristic zero). A subring of a domain is a domain, so $Q_i$ is integral.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, quotients; VI Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.5, pp.73--74

proof.text: Verify the characteristic of every quotient stratum, for either coordinate system $v=t$ or $t'$. Its source rank-$r$ locus is the disjoint union, over $|S|=r$ with $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n_a\}$, of $V(v_i:i\in S)\setminus\bigcup_{j\notin S,\ j\leq n_a}V(v_j)$. Each is nonempty integral: its ring is the localization of $C[[v_j:j\notin S]]$ obtained by inverting the other boundary variables. It is closed in the rank-$r$ locus, and with finitely many such pieces it is also open there. Its generic point has characteristic zero, since this domain contains the Cohen ring $C$, which has characteristic zero. Kummer characteristic maps have equal group ranks (injectivity and a positive multiple of every target element in the image give equal rational spans), so quotient rank loci have exactly these inverse images. Diagonal $H$ preserves each coordinate pattern. Orbit fibres make their images disjoint, and finiteness makes each image closed in the quotient rank locus. Thus these integral images are precisely its connected components. A source generic point maps to the generic point of its integral image; the injection of residue fields preserves characteristic, proving the claim for every quotient stratum. For residue characteristic zero, $\mathbf Q\subset A$ and hence $\mathbf Q\subset A^H$, so every quotient point has characteristic zero directly.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, p.128, maximal points of quotient log strata have characteristic zero

proof.text: Finish the induction promised in Step 1. For each chosen component define $U_i=G\times^H X_i$ and $Y_i^{\rm ind}=G\times^H Y_i$ as copies indexed by $G/H$: $[g,x]\mapsto g x$ defines $h_i$, and $[g,x]\mapsto[g,j_i(x)]$ defines $j_i^{\rm ind}$. This is well-defined since $(gh,x)$ is identified with $(g,hx)$ and $j_i$ is $H$-equivariant. A geometric stabilizer of $[g,x]$ is $gH_xg^{-1}$; the corresponding stabilizer in $X$ is $gG_xg^{-1}=gH_xg^{-1}$ by Step 1. The same computation, with inertness of $j_i$, treats the other map. Each copy of $X_i$ maps isomorphically to a component of $X$ and the chosen orbit representatives make $h=\coprod h_i$ surjective etale. Finite coproducts of affine spectra are affine and separated (the affine diagonal is the closed immersion induced by the surjective multiplication map); $j=\coprod j_i^{\rm ind}$ is a closed immersion of finite coproducts. Transport the three divisors to every copy. Their pullback equations, strictness, regularity, very tameness, free complement and abelian tame inertia are checked on the copies. Distinct translates of an $E$ component either coincide or lie in disjoint copies, proving $G$-strictness. Finally $(G\times^H Y_i)/G=Y_i/H$: on invariant functions an invariant tuple is determined by its identity-coset entry in $R^H$. The same statement for invariant log sections identifies both induced log quotients with the local quotients of Steps 9--10. Their finite disjoint union has every claimed property. For $m=0$ all schemes and divisors are empty; for $d=0$ the positive-characteristic piece is $\operatorname{Spec}C$, and all empty products and parameter lists used above have their stated meanings.

source.place: VIII 5.5.2, final paragraph, p.128; VIII 5.3.7, induction of actions, p.124
